title: Joint Survivor Direct and Spillover Effect Regions under Monotone Survival over Exposure Posets
banked_reason: D0.5.G assessed subfield at paper score ceiling 7.3 below the field floor 7.4; mathematics passed, positioning was corrected and independently re-reviewed clean, but no bounded same-topic repair reaches field.
gap_reasons: The closed-form headline is sharp only under the focal mean-marginal information contract, while the paper's own counterexample shows that full within-dyad observables can collapse that region and are handled only through a generic finite LP.
The all-edge construction is exponential outside fixed-width posets, and the fixed-width result establishes formulation size and membership rather than statistical inference from estimated margins.

The absence of inference theory, software or an applied demonstration, together with novelty resting partly on a negative literature search, limits the projected leading-journal score despite the exact identification results.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the Boolean-square sharp joint region, redundancy criterion, finite-poset common-terminal shortest-path characterization, fixed-width all-edge formulation, and an exact binary full-dyad LP/losslessness theorem; the math referee passed the package. The field claim collapsed at novelty review because its strongest closed form uses only mean marginals, richer observables retain a generic finite LP, and the package has no inference or applied layer. The run stopped before Lean formalization, leaving the discharged derivation and construction artifacts for a future re-raised project rather than an accepted formal paper.
tldr: The proposal asks which combinations of survivor direct and spillover effects can arise from one common latent response law when survival is monotone over an exposure poset. Its main claim to investigate is that the Boolean square has exactly two compatibility facets beyond four separately sharp scalar intervals, with observable redundancy criteria and constructive witnesses; more generally, common-terminal effects have an exact shortest-path region with a threshold-coupling lift, while all-edge targets admit a fixed-width up-set formulation. This matters because multiplying valid scalar SACE bounds can admit scientifically impossible joint conclusions, and existing scalar interference bounds or ordinal-chain polytopes do not resolve compatibility across incomparable exposures and differently conditioned survivor strata.
gap: Scalar truncation bounds characterize one ordered exposure pair at a time, while the closest joint SACE work assumes an ordinal chain and no interference. Neither literature gives the simultaneous region for the Boolean exposure square or the causal projection for a finite partial order. The validity of the square result is explicitly limited to focal exposure-specific marginal laws; whether full within-dyad observables add restrictions remains unresolved.
fill: Prove a closed-form Boolean theorem with exactly two overlap facets, iff redundancy, exact duals, and full-vector laws; prove the finite-poset common-terminal path theorem and constructive lift; and establish an exact up-set formulation with fixed-width complexity for all-edge targets. Treat the richer dyad law as a separate research question rather than silently claiming sharpness for it.
